what_its_for: Fostamatinib is used to treat low platelet counts (a condition called chronic immune thrombocytopenia, or ITP) in adults who have already tried other treatments that did not work well enough. Platelets are tiny blood cells that help your blood clot when you have a cut or injury. This medicine helps raise your platelet count to reduce your risk of serious bleeding.
how_to_take: Take fostamatinib by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Try to take your doses at the same times each day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another tablet — just take your next scheduled dose as usual.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg (one tablet) taken twice a day, about 12 hours apart. Your doctor may increase your dose to 150 mg twice a day after about 4 weeks if your platelet count has not improved enough and you are tolerating the medicine well. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed and do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still more than 6 hours before your next scheduled dose. If it is less than 6 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store fostamatinib tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect them from moisture and heat. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid taking certain antibiotics, antifungals, or seizure medicines without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as they can interfere with how fostamatinib works. Do not start any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements without telling your healthcare team first. Avoid activities that could cause injury or bruising, since your platelet count may still be low during treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: unusual or severe bleeding (such as blood in your urine or stool, vomiting blood, or bleeding that will not stop); very high blood pressure (severe headache, blurred vision, chest pain, or shortness of breath); signs of liver problems (yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness); signs of infection (fever, chills, body aches); or severe diarrhea that does not get better. Also tell your doctor if you become pregnant or are planning to become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Your platelet count will be checked regularly with blood tests during your treatment. Some patients begin to see improvement in their platelet counts within 4 to 8 weeks. Your doctor will monitor your response and decide whether to continue, adjust, or stop the medicine based on your results. It may take up to 12 weeks to know if fostamatinib is working well for you.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Fostamatinib can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 month after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 1 month after stopping. Liver problems: If you have moderate or severe liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. Older adults: Older patients can take this medicine, but they may be more sensitive to side effects such as high blood pressure and should be monitored carefully.
